question.leadin: This government was headed by Philippe Petain.
question.text: Name this Nazi-approved government that ruled France from a namesake city during World War II, while the Germans occupied Paris.
question.answerHtml: Vichy France [or the French State; or État français; prompt on France]
question.clue: It held the Vel'd'hiv raids, which sent people to the Drancy camp, and ran under the motto of "Work, Family, Fatherland".

swap.text: English forces under Henry V utilized the longbow during this battle, which took place during St. Crispin's Day. During this battle, French forces under Charles d'Albret got stuck in muddy terrain.
swap.clue: Action began when the English abandoned their prepared positions, and rain had turned the newly ploughed fields into mud, while the field was hemmed in by forests on two sides.

question.leadin: Give the following about French diplomat Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand.
question.text: The French Revolution ended with the rise of this friend of Talleyrand as First Consul of France. This manlater became the French Emperor.
question.clue: This man signed the Concordat of 1801 with Pope Pius VII (the seventh), who had earlier crowned him in a lavish ceremony.

swap.leadin: This commander claimed to be able to hear St. Margaret and St. Catherine speaking to her.
swap.text: Name this peasant girl, who commanded French troops to victory in the Siege of Orleans ["orr-lee-ON"]. She was later burned at the stake by the English.
swap.clue: This commander encouraged Charles VII ("the seventh") to be crowned at Reims ("RONCE").

question.text: The massacre was instigated by this Queen Mother of France, a member of the Medici family, who claimed that it was necessary to stave off a Protestant coup.
question.clue: This person is quoted as saying "peace is carried on a stick" when convincing Henry III to go to war against the Catholic League.

swap.leadin: During the Affair of the Placards, members of this denomination placed posters in several French cities, including on the door of Francis I's bedchamber at Amboise.
swap.text: Name this denomination whose freedom was guaranteed by Henry IV in the Edict of Nantes. Many members of this denomination followed the teachings of John Calvin, the author of Institutes of the Christian Religion.
swap.clue: The war began because Henry III did not want Henry of Navarre, who belonged to this religious sect, to be his heir. French members of this sect were known as Huguenots.

question.leadin: This man clashed with Odo the Great over control of Aquitaine, but worked with him during one battle.
question.text: Name this Frankish leader who defeated an Umayyad army at the Battle of Tours. His nickname means "hammer."
question.answerHtml: Charles Martel [prompt on Charles , do not accept or prompt on "Martel"]
question.clue: He supported the missionary work of St. Boniface, and was imprisoned by his father's widow Plectrude.

swap.leadin: The tide of this battle is alleged to have turned when the losing side ran from the battlefield in order to protect their camp and all the loot inside.
swap.text: Name this battle in which Frankish infantry defeated forces under Abd ar-Rahman. It took place after an appeal by Odo the Great as an invading force approached the River Loire.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Tours (or the Battle of Poitiers; or the Battle of the Palace of the Martyrs)
swap.clue: The opposing forces in this battle met between the Clain and Vienne rivers, and it occurred near the village of Moussais-la-bataille.

question.leadin: Snoopy always fought against the Red Baron. Answer these questions on World War I.
question.text: This engagement lasted from February to July of 1916 in which General Petain stalled the advance of General von Falkenhayn. 400,000 French and as many Germans lost their lives.
question.clue: This battle was preceded by one side's capture of Fort Douaumont, and the fighting in this battle took place mostly on and around the banks of the Meuse River.

swap.text: The French armies returned from the war to repress this disorder provoked by the Parlement of Paris; a second version with noble support broke out in 1650.
swap.clue: Noble members of the parlements began this event by refusing to pay higher taxes during the Franco-Spanish War.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the foremost legal battle of the French Third Republic.
question.text: This French socialist leader and cofounder of the newspaper L'Humanite campaigned hard for Revision with his book Les Preuves; backlash from it cost him his seat in the Chamber of Deputies.
question.answer: Auguste Marie Joseph Jean Leon Jaures
question.clue: The Socialist Party which Blum joined had been founded in 1905 from a disparate coalition of splinter groups by this cofounder of the newspaper L'Humanite, who in 1914 was assassinated for his pacifism.

swap.leadin: Name these things that went on in France in the 1950s.
swap.text: The constitution of this republic was adopted on October 13, 1946. It gave the second chamber of the legislature, the "Council of the Republic," a weak voice, and was ended by in favor of a new state under Charles de Gaulle.

question.leadin: The French Third Republic was best by a series of political scandals in the late nineteenth century.
question.text: Though this man successfully wrangled Egyptian concessions and planned the building of the Suez Canal, his involvement in Panama was a debacle which ended with his conviction for defrauding investors and bribing politicians.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about medieval monastic reform movements.
swap.text: This Benedictine monastery developed a large network of daughter monasteries in the 10th and 11th centuries under the abbots Odilo, Hugh the Great and Peter the Venerable. It was also home to the largest church in the world until the construction of New St. Peters.
swap.clue: A head of this institution spearheaded the Truce of the Peace of God movement.

question.leadin: During this event, a woman called La Voisin ("vwah-ZANN") confessed to having murdered no fewer than 2,500 infants.
question.text: Name this sensational event in French history that exposed the fact that many members of French society had been hiring female fortune-tellers for criminal purposes. This event implicated the Madame de Montespan ("mon-teh-SPAWN").
question.answerHtml: Affair of the Poisons [or L’affaire des poisons]
question.clue: As Lieutenant-General of the Police, de la Reynie investigated this scandal that exposed many French aristocrats for hiring fortune tellers for illicit purposes. The king's mistress Madame de Montespan was implicated in this scandal.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about political changes in the year 2012.
swap.text: This far right-wing party's candidate in the French 2012 elections, Marine Le Pen, received eighteen percent of the vote in the first round, falling behind Francois Hollande and Nicolas Sarkozy. It is the third-largest political party in France.
swap.clue: Marine Le Pen will stand for this ultra-right-wing party, which her father Jean-Marie founded. Her rhetoric has been anti-European and anti-immigration, but she has tried to distance her party from extremism.

question.leadin: The nascent French Second Republic's guarantee of a "right to work" ultimately played a part in destabilizing that government.
question.text: The right to work was to be guaranteed by National Workshops, workers' organizations paid by the government for public works projects, a project championed by this French socialist and historian.
question.answerHtml: Louis Blanc [do not accept Louis Blanqui, a different person]
question.clue: One notable politician who had opposed the rise of the famous Napoleon III was this French socialist, who tried to implement a program of public workshops after the revolution of 1848. He supported the right of citizens to be able to work.

swap.text: Louis the Lion, the victor at the Battle of Roche-au-Moine, was a member of this French royal house, as was his father, Philip II.

question.leadin: FTPE, answer the following about some angry responses to the French Revolution.
question.text: The Chouans, who were centered primarily in Brittany and Normandy, joined the revolting Catholic peasants in this region's eponymous 1793 rebellion against the Revolutionary government, which was put down brutally.
question.clue: A historiographical controversy over this region intensified in 1986 when Reynald Secher claimed that it was the site of the "first modern genocide."

swap.leadin: This man paid a visit to Louis XVIII in the Low Countries, earning the pejorative nickname "The Man of Ghent."
swap.text: Name this man who loomed large over pre-1848 French politics as a jack-of-all-trades minister to Citizen King Louis Philippe.
swap.clue: Fernando Pereira was killed during an operation ordered by this president's government.
